stack.text: BRIGHTWORK STUDIO
Data Centers Worldwide
Cloud regions and AI campuses, October 2026
Summary

Two kinds of data center are growing at once, and they are built for different reasons. Cloud regions are the established kind: Amazon, Microsoft and Google list 132 between them, in 76 metro areas across six areas of the world. AI campuses are the new kind: single sites that draw hundreds of megawatts. Epoch AI tracks 93, and the 72 that are already running draw 13.7 GW of IT power, 86% of it in the United States.

Two kinds of data center
Cloud region
A group of data centers in one metro area, split into zones that fail independently.
Rented by the hour. Customers pick a region for speed, or for the law: some data must stay in its country.
Counted in regions and zones. The providers do not publish building counts.
AI campus
One site built around a single very large cluster of accelerator chips, to train and run AI models.
Placed where a lot of power can be had quickly, not where the customers are.
Counted in megawatts of IT power. The figures are Epoch AI's estimates, from permits, satellite images and company statements.
Cloud regions

Counts are as listed in each provider's documentation in October 2026. The three lists overlap on purpose: the same metro areas, such as Northern Virginia, London, Tokyo and Singapore, appear in all three. 35 of the 76 metro areas have regions from more than one provider.

Azure lists the most regions, but 17 of its 57 have no availability zones and 8 are open only by request, so it lists fewer zones than Google, which has 41 regions and 124 zones. Asia Pacific has the most regions of any area, 43, ahead of Europe with 38 and North America with 31. Africa and South America have the fewest.
AI campuses

The largest running campus is Colossus 2, at 946 MW of IT power, ahead of Amazon New Carlisle and Fairwater Atlanta. Most of the growth is still to come. If the plans hold, the 81 campuses on the map reach about 32 GW by 2029, more than twice what runs today. Outside the United States, Johor in Malaysia is the biggest hub, with two campuses and 895 MW, ahead of China with 731 MW. Planned power is Epoch AI's estimate of the full build-out.
Largest running campuses

9 campuses show no running capacity yet. Most of them plan close to a gigawatt or more by 2028: Meta's Hyperion in Louisiana, and the Stargate sites in New Mexico, Texas, Michigan and Wisconsin and in Abu Dhabi.
Under construction
What it means
Cloud regions follow people. They sit in metro areas with many customers, and the lists now include recent regions in new countries: Mexico, Chile, Malaysia, New Zealand and Thailand.

AI campuses follow power. They tend to sit in smaller places such as Abilene, New Albany and Pryor, where land is cheaper and large grid connections are available. That concentrates them: 86% of running power is in one country.
The map on the last page shows both. Cloud regions spread across the metro areas of the world. AI campuses cluster, and most of them are in the United States.
Sources and method

Cloud regions: the AWS Regions table (docs.aws.amazon.com), the Azure regions list (learn.microsoft.com) and the Google Cloud regions and zones table (docs.cloud.google.com), read in October 2026. AWS's own tally is 39 regions and 124 availability zones, because it also counts regions that need a separate account, such as GovCloud. We use the 34 in its account documentation.

AI campuses: Epoch AI, "AI data centers", epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers, licensed CC BY 4.0, retrieved in October 2026. Epoch tracks 93 campuses. 81 are on the map: the 72 that run today and the 9 under construction. The other 12 draw no power yet and are left off.
Epoch gives addresses, not coordinates. We placed each marker by hand, at town level for campuses and metro level for cloud regions, so a marker can be off by a few kilometers.
